boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on nearby Schenectady corridors, each with a specific documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Jay Street Marketplace
cards.subtitle: Jay Street pedestrian corridor
cards.notes: Walk the cobblestone pedestrian stretch and pause at the specialty shops and places to eat listed by Union.
cards.evidence_claim: Union College describes Jay Street as a cobblestone walkway lined with specialty shops and places to eat.
cards.access_notes: Public pedestrian corridor; individual businesses set their own access and purchase terms.

cards.title: Movieland 6 Cinema
cards.subtitle: State Street corridor
cards.notes: Check the current listings, then plan a film outing with standard cinema concessions available on site.
cards.short_summary: A downtown cinema for current film screenings.
cards.evidence_claim: Union College identifies Movieland 6 Cinema as a place to catch current Hollywood films and buy concession items.
cards.access_notes: Confirm showtimes and ticket availability with the cinema before going.

cards.title: Tara Kitchen
cards.subtitle: Liberty Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s location page to confirm the Schenectady address and current dinner service before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A walk-in Moroccan restaurant on Liberty Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Tara Kitchen lists its Schenectady location at 431 Liberty Street and identifies it as walk-in service.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists Tuesday–Sunday dinner service; verify before travel.

cards.title: Proctors
cards.subtitle: State Street corridor
cards.notes: Look at the performance calendar and choose a show; the building includes several theatres and a training center.
cards.short_summary: A multi-space performing-arts stop on State Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Proctors states that its building at 432 State Street contains several theatres, a training center, rental spaces and a café.
cards.access_notes: Performance admission and building access vary by event; consult the venue calendar.

cards.title: Schenectady Greenmarket
cards.subtitle: Jay Street / City Hall corridor
cards.notes: Check the market schedule, then browse local vendors for food and other goods in downtown Schenectady.
cards.short_summary: A local-vendor market near the Jay Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Union College identifies the Schenectady Greenmarket as a local shopping-and-eating option near campus.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current market date, location and vendors before visiting.

cards.title: Arthur's Market
cards.subtitle: North Ferry Street, beside the Stockade corridor
cards.notes: Pair a Stockade walk with a stop for coffee or baked goods, as suggested on Union’s local guide.
cards.short_summary: A Stockade-adjacent market stop for coffee and baked goods.
cards.evidence_claim: Union College’s Stockade recommendation specifically directs visitors to Arthur’s Market for coffee and baked goods.
cards.access_notes: Food and beverage purchases are optional; confirm current service before visiting.

cards.title: Mohawk-Hudson Bike-Hike Trail
cards.subtitle: Riverfront and Washington Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Enter from a suitable access point and follow the route through the county, including the downtown and riverfront sections.
cards.short_summary: A regional trail that links downtown, riverfront and historic-route segments.
cards.evidence_claim: Schenectady County says the trail runs through downtown’s business and entertainment district and includes a riverfront ALCO Heritage Trail section.
cards.source_title: Empire State Trail/Mohawk-Hudson Bike-Hike Trail | Schenectady County
cards.access_notes: Use the county trail map and follow posted route, etiquette and street-crossing guidance.

cards.title: Schenectady Historical Museum
cards.subtitle: Washington Avenue, Stockade corridor
cards.notes: Start at the museum to explore Schenectady County history through exhibits, programs or a scheduled Stockade walking tour.
cards.short_summary: A history-museum starting point in the Stockade.
cards.evidence_claim: The Schenectady County Historical Society describes its museum as a starting point for exploring county history through programs and exhibits.
cards.source_title: Museum & Library - Schenectady County Historical Society
cards.access_notes: The museum lists admission and hours; library research appointments must be scheduled in advance.

cards.title: Central Park Rose Garden
cards.subtitle: Central Park / Rugby Road corridor
cards.notes: Take a garden walk, stay on paths and respect the plantings, water features, sculptures and other public visitors.
cards.short_summary: A public rose garden inside Central Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Schenectady lists a Rose Garden among Central Park’s features, and its garden rules state that it is open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Public access is documented; photography-for-hire and rentals have separate city permit or fee rules.

cards.title: Robb Alley
cards.subtitle: State Street corridor, inside Proctors
cards.notes: Pass through the public alley connecting State Street, the box office and Apostrophe Café while you explore the Proctors block.
cards.short_summary: A public passage through the Proctors building.
cards.evidence_claim: Proctors describes Robb Alley as a public space with access from State Street, the box office and Apostrophe Café.
cards.access_notes: Access may be affected by venue operations or events; check with Proctors if planning a specific visit.
